scenarios.expected: A filesystem failure after backup movement retains the staged update, restores previous active bundle bytes and reports retained paths; an explicit later retry can install the reviewed update.
limitations: Controlled macOS filesystem/process intervention, not a spontaneous field failure or Linux recovery observation. No production hook, service mock or internal API substitution was used.

scenarios.observed: After the backup appeared and active path was absent, the operator applied the controlled filesystem fault. Update exited 2 with a filesystem error and retained-stage diagnostic. The original active bundle was restored byte-for-byte; all preexisting project files were preserved, with only the 502-file retained stage added. After removing the operator flag, retry exited 0 with applied=true and installed pinned v2; the failed stage remained byte-identical.
steps: Adopt a disposable generic project and import a locally authored 500-template v1 bundle through the actual CLI and file-only Git routing.
Start reviewed v2 update; observe its real backup path, stop the owned process, snapshot the complete stage and backup, apply a macOS user-immutable flag to the staged directory and resume.
Capture failed CLI exit and retained-path diagnostic; compare restored active bundle and all preexisting project bytes.
Remove only the operator-applied flag, retain all paths, and run the same reviewed update again.
